To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new approach to the synthesis of porous polymers with pore sizes as small as ∼1.0 nm and with chemical interior of the pores that is tunable by chemical treatment.

the nanoporous polymeric materials are prepared by polymerization of a discotic liquid crystal monomer and that the pore size and chemical interior of the pores can be tailored by further chemical treatment.

the pore diameter of the nanoporous polymeric network can be tailored to be ∼1.2–2.5 nm, and the pore interior is lined with functional groups, including −NH3+, −N3, −Ph, −COONH2, −COO−, and −COO−Na+, that can be changed by simple chemical reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and chemical modification of nanoporous polymers with near 1 nm sized pores lined with functional surface groups.
the design of a disc-shaped triazine based molecule that can form a Colhex LC phase.
the synthesis of a nanoporous polymer with a well-defined pore structure and surface functionalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated the ability to tailor pore size and the chemical interior of near 1nm sized pores in a nanoporous polymer based on a discotic LC.
the nanoporous polymer with 2.6 nm diameter pores lined with −SO3Na surface groups selectively adsorbed the cationic dye (MB) over the anionic dye (methylene green) in aqueous solutions.
the Colhex ordered discotic LC monomer was successfully polymerized via ADMET to create a nanoporous polymer with a pore size of ∼1.4 nm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we could fabricate a nanoporous polymer based on a discotic LC, and the pore size could be tailored from near 1 to ∼2.8 nm by chemical modification, while maintaining the LC order.
we have demonstrated a new strategy for the fabrication of a nanoporous polymer with near 1 nm sized pores lined with ammonium and anionic functional groups at the pore surfaces.

a nanoporous polymer with a near 1 nm pore diameter lined with a variety of functional groups can be fabricated by chemical treatment of an imine based discotic liquid crystal polymer in the Colhex phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new strategy to create nanoporous polymers lined with a wide variety of chemical groups at the pore surfaces.
the pore size and the chemical interior of the pores can be tailored by a combination of polymerization, chemical reactions, and hydrolysis of imine and esters.

the Colhex phase of a discotic triazine based monomer is an ideal template for the fabrication of nanoporous polymers with near 1 nm sized pores lined with various functional groups at the pore surfaces.
